_source: MMG_v19_Client_Manual_Testing_Guideline_FG15-FG20_v1.0.xlsx / Testing Guideline — pulled from the client's Drive on 2026-09-16, now canonical in mmg/document. FG-16 'Odoo Studio Layer & Legal-Date Compliance' holds 4 cases: TC-STU-006, TC-STU-012, TC-LEG-005, TC-LEG-006. All 4 are implemented.
_target: Odoo 19 only. The question FG-16 asks — did the old system's Studio layer survive the upgrade — has no meaning against v15.
_safety: TC-LEG-005 and TC-LEG-006 build their own orders, deliveries and invoices. That is not fastidiousness: validating a delivery is irreversible and stamps a legal sale date, and TC-LEG-006 needs an invoice POSTED, so borrowing the gallery's orders would write to their books. TC-STU-006's step 5 does touch the gallery's own records, but only to write a field back onto itself — the workbook's own definition of a trivial edit — because the save is the fact under test.
_cleanup: A POSTED invoice can never be deleted in Odoo, and neither can anything an account.move.line points at, so the product behind TC-LEG-006's posted branch is permanently undeletable the moment the case does its job. Those rows are ARCHIVED and the cleanup asserts that no LIVE record is left; sweep() retries deletion of previously archived rows on every run, so anything that later becomes deletable does go.

_findings.BC-FG16-001 [RESOLVED]: FIXED 2026-09-16. 'Inventory > Operations' was active but gated on base.group_no_one, so the whole branch - Transfers, Deliveries, Receipts, Adjustments including Physical Inventory, and Scrap - reached nobody without Technical Features. The gate was in the DATABASE, not the code: Odoo 19 declares the menu with no groups attribute (addons/stock/views/stock_menu_views.xml:7) and so does Odoo 15 (checked in mmg_15/addons), and nothing in mmg_19-custom touches it - somebody set it by hand on the v15 production database and the restore carried it forward. Removed via the ORM, not SQL, because _visible_menu_ids/load_menus are ormcached and a raw UPDATE leaves the running workers serving the old tree. Menus served went from 233 to 243 and all three cases that failed on it - TC-STU-006, TC-SMK-003, TC-UIX-011 - now pass. Made reproducible in mmg_19-custom/tools/staging19_cleanup.sh step 4g as a third direction, WANT_UNGATED, beside WANT_ON/WANT_OFF, with step 6 verifying it (expect 0 rows), so a fresh staging rebuild reapplies it. NOT swept: the six other menus this database gates the same way - Languages, Database Structure, CRM Tags, Lost Reasons and two Configuration > Products menus - are clutter-hiding and look deliberate, so they are deliberately left alone. ORIGINAL FINDING: P1, and it fails TC-STU-006. 'Inventory > Operations' is gated on base.group_no_one on this database, so the whole branch — Transfers, Deliveries, Receipts, Adjustments (including Physical Inventory) and Scrap — is invisible under Inventory unless developer mode is on. Stock Odoo 19 declares that menu with NO groups attribute (addons/stock/views/stock_menu_views.xml:7-10) and nothing in mmg_19-custom touches it, so the restriction came across in the restored database rather than from code; 75 menus on this database carry base.group_no_one. Consequence beyond this case: it is also the navigation FG-12's TC-FUL-013 tells the tester to use ('Inventory > Operations > Transfers > Deliveries'). Reported by TEST-FG16-STU-006, which FAILS on it — the workbook's Expected Result is explicit that one unreachable screen fails the case however well the others behaved.
_findings.OBS-FG16-001: sale.order and account.move each carry TWO fields labelled 'Legal Sale Date': the live datetime pair (x_legal_sale_date / x_legal_invoice_date) that mmg_legal_date maintains, and the older Studio date pair (x_slsdate / x_lsdate) the v15 automations wrote. TC-LEG-005 step 2 expects both on the invoice form, so this is the documented state, not a defect — but two fields with one label on one form is worth the Controller's attention alongside FG-16 D5's proposal to retire the legacy pair.
_findings.OBS-FG16-002: FG-16 D5, for the Controller: editing an order's Legal Sale Date rewrites the legal date of a POSTED invoice. Verified live — the value moved and the invoice stayed posted. This reproduces v15's automated action 664, whose guard `state not in ('paid','cancel')` reduces to `state != 'cancel'`. The workbook says to record it and flag it as a decision, not judge it, so the test asserts the shipped behaviour. If the answer is 'a posted invoice must be frozen', the change is one line: mmg_legal_date/models/sale_order.py:88 becomes `return invoice.state != 'draft'`.

TC-STU-006.reason: PASSES as of 2026-09-16. It used to FAIL on BC-FG16-001, now fixed: 'Inventory > Operations' no longer carries base.group_no_one and the whole branch is served. All ten screens open and every view behind them builds, which is what an 'Invalid view definition' pop-up actually is; the extra gallery columns are on their lists, the three product tabs and the Notes tab are on their forms, and all four trivial saves complete. Screens are reached through ir.ui.menu.load_menus — the call the web client makes — rather than by XML id, which is exactly why screen (i) was caught: a test written against stock.action_view_quants would have passed while the tester could not reach the screen. Step 6 (two PDFs) is residual manual.

TC-STU-012.reason: All six Studio contact fields exist with exactly the labels the workbook prints, are on the form, take the workbook's own Test Data and read it back unchanged, accept a second edit that leaves the other five alone, and Customer Type and Main Phone are columns on the contacts list. A contact carried over from the old system is checked for its original Customer Type.

TC-LEG-005.reason: End to end on scratch records: a confirmed order with an empty legal date and an invoice with an empty one, its delivery validated, and the order's Legal Sale Date then equal to the delivery's Effective Date to the minute with the invoice carrying the same value. Both fields labelled 'Legal Sale Date' are confirmed on the invoice form as step 2 describes.

TC-LEG-006.reason: All three branches built here — draft, posted and cancelled invoices on three scratch orders. The draft follows the order immediately; the posted one also moves and is recorded as OBS-FG16-002 rather than judged, as the workbook instructs; the cancelled one does not move. The original values are put back on all three orders, per step 8. Step 7 (the PDF line) is residual manual.
